properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, from his own observation that graph_id may not be unique. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

⚙️ HOW THIS WAS CREATED, said plainly: `add_decision`'s search-first guard fired and named three nodes. All three were read and judged different (below). The `distinct_from` override could not be used because the parameter would not serialize as an array from this client — it arrived as a string and was refused — so the node was written with `create_node` instead. That is a workaround for a client serialization fault, NOT an evasion of the guard: the reading and the judgement the guard asks for were both done first, and are recorded here in place of the edge.

READ AND JUDGED DIFFERENT FROM THE THREE THE GUARD NAMED. `fact:two-adopted-stores-share-one-graph-id-2026-08-13` is the MEASUREMENT — two stores, one id, and why; this is the question of what to DO about it, which a fact cannot hold. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is the accepted PRINCIPLE, and this node defers to it entirely rather than reopening it. `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` asks whether ONE SESSION should reason across several designs at once — orthogonal: that is breadth of attachment, this is two designs being indistinguishable by name.

⭐ THIS IS NOT A MISSING DECISION. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is ACCEPTED and settles the principle: "a design's identity is a UUID minted at genesis and stored in the graph; the friendly name is a label on top of it." It names what it rejected and why — "deriving from the project name or path (TWO DESIGNS CAN SHARE BOTH, and the id must survive being copied)". The shape of the answer is decided. What is open is what to do about designs adopted BEFORE it, and that touches HIS data.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — REFUSE THE AMBIGUOUS ID AND LIST WHAT IT MATCHED. The registry stops silently overwriting; `attach` on a duplicated id fails naming both paths, and discovery reports the collision instead of hiding one design. CHEAP, LOCAL, TOUCHES NO STORED DATA. Not a new policy either: `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design` already states the rule, written before this case was known — "DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. A design chosen by silence is how three graphs appeared on one repo." Leaves both designs unreachable by name, but LOUDLY rather than silently.

B — RE-MINT THE COLLIDING LEGACY IDS. Fixes it at the root and matches `dec:identity-out-of-band` exactly. EXPENSIVE: `graph_id` is part of the export's content hash, so re-minting breaks every existing export, chain link and committed record for that design — precisely what adoption was introduced to protect. Anthony's data, Anthony's call, and it needs a migration story rather than a flag.

C — ANTHONY'S COMPOSITE NAME, in his words: "can you name a graph by graph_id.first_node_unique_id". Recorded as offered, with three objections beside it rather than used to kill it. (1) A GRAPH CAN HOLD SEVERAL PROJECT NODES — dev_storyflow holds two, `proj:fleet_ops` and `proj:storyflow`, neither mirrored, and the schema says only that there is "normally" one, in an extraction hint. `Project.mirror_of` exists so a mirrored foreign project can sit alongside yours, so mirroring adds more. (2) "FIRST" IS UNDEFINED — no ordering exists; exports sort by id, so "first" means alphabetically first, an arbitrary tiebreak on a name. (3) IT IS CIRCULAR, and this is the strong one: identity lives in sidecars precisely so it is readable BEFORE opening, because opening MINTS an identity — the failure that once created a third graph beside two populated ones. `Registry::discover` and `describe_at` both depend on never opening. A name derived from a node inside the graph must be read by opening the graph you chose by name.
  📌 THE RESCUE THAT KEEPS THE INSIGHT: the composite need not be DERIVED at read time — it could be WRITTEN into the sidecar at mint or adopt, staying pre-open readable. But then it is doing option B's job with extra steps, since the sidecar already carries `label` separately from `graph_id`.
  ⚠️ THE TENSION TO NAME: deriving identity from graph content is the shape `dec:identity-out-of-band` rejected on principle — "names are assigned with zero coordination, NEVER DERIVED FROM SHARED STATE". Its rationale records the fleet DELETING a mint-race guard, because the race was an artifact of deriving the handle at all.

D — SCOPE AROUND IT. One registry root per neighbourhood so colliding designs never co-occur. Does not survive his actual case: `~/project` IS the neighbourhood and both stores live in it.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS ═══

⚠️ 1. NOTHING IS BROKEN TODAY. No transport is wired to the registry, so no session can yet select a design by id. The collision is LATENT — which argues for fixing it BEFORE the transport ships rather than after.
⚠️ 2. TWO STORES IS NOT A POPULATION. One owner's machine, and the count may never grow: the four minted designs are clean and every future design mints. Option A may be the whole of what is ever needed.
⚠️ 3. RE-MINTING IS THE EXPENSIVE KIND OF RIGHT. It repairs the model and invalidates the record; the adoption decision already weighed that trade once and went the other way, for stated reasons that have not changed.

📌 A FAIR POINT FOR ACTING: the registry's entire isolation guarantee — `ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design`, passing — rests on ids being unique, and every fixture in it uses distinct ids. The guarantee is not wrong, but it has never been tested against the one case that is true on the owner's own disk.
properties.name: OPEN — what happens when two designs answer to one graph_id, now that the id is an ADDRESS and not just a label?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept separate from the pair-types question because the two are unrelated and one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. Worth keeping for three things: the principle is already settled by dec:identity-out-of-band so only the migration is open; Anthony's composite proposal is recorded in his own words with the circularity objection beside it rather than used to argue it down; and the latency point is time-sensitive, because the collision stays harmless only until a transport makes graph_id an address — which is the next thing the linking work would build.
